subject: Operator Bridge POC: attestation checklist and network gating
messages:
From: Kendall Reyes <kendall@datasyn.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: DataSyn Security <security@datasyn.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operator Bridge POC & attestation checklist

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to proceed to a short POC that will prove we can use our on-prem HSM (Thales nShield) for signing and key origination while Redwood Private runs in our VPC. Two items we need to validate up-front:

1) Attestation: We need a reproducible attestation flow so our security team can verify that operator processes accessing the HSM are running from an attested, immutable image and that no key material leaves our network.
2) Network gating and credentials: We need clear guidance on how Redwood will connect to the HSM (port/protocol, client certs), whether a proxy or “operator bridge” is required in our DMZ, and how to limit egress and firewall rules.

I've attached our baseline security questionnaire and a brief diagram of our network. Can you share a checklist for the POC and a short runbook for the attestation flow?

Kendall
Kendall Reyes
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer, DataSyn Analytics

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operator Bridge POC & attestation checklist

Kendall — thanks, this is a great starting point. High-level approach and what we'll validate in the POC below. See attached POC diagram and an initial attestation checklist.

POC goals (2-week run):
- Demonstrate operator bridge that establishes an ephemeral, attested session from Redwood Private to your HSM.
- Show that signing operations are performed inside your HSM (no plaintext key egress).
- Produce audit logs and a signed attestation document (hash of environment + operator binary + ephemeral session ID).

Pattern overview (short):
- Operator bridge: a lightweight agent you deploy in your VPC (customer-owned) that exposes a limited gRPC interface to Redwood's control plane over mutual TLS. The bridge authenticates with the HSM using PKCS#11 and performs crypto ops on behalf of tenant namespaces.
- Attestation: the bridge runs inside an attested container/VM (customer choice — TPM-based remote attestation or SGX attestation). Bridge generates an ephemeral TLS client cert derived from an attested key; Redwood verifies the attestation statement (quote) before allowing any session.
- Key material handling: keys remain in the HSM. Redwood stores only sealed blobs (opaque references) and session metadata. Sealed blobs are encrypted with a per-customer wrapping key that is derived by the HSM for escrow scenarios.
- Network gating: we recommend a minimal outbound rule set (Redwood control-plane IPs + port 443 for the bridge). No inbound rules to internal networks; bridge initiates connections.

High-level checklist attached: attestation-checklist.xlsx. Next steps if you agree: we scope an initial network lab (security review) and schedule an on-site/remote run of the POC.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Operator Bridge POC & attestation checklist

Kendall, quick technical clarifications from the infra side so we can prepare the runbook: 

Network and connectivity notes:
- Connectivity model: bridge is customer-run inside their VPC. It makes an outbound, mutual-TLS (mTLS) connection to Redwood's dedicated ingestion edge (no public internet egress required beyond that single outbound flow if you use a PrivateLink/Transit Gateway).
- Ports/protocols: gRPC over TLS (443). HSM connectivity stays local (PKCS#11 over internal network). If your HSM requires a separate signing appliance, the bridge will talk to it over the HSM vendor ports (we'll list exact ports once you confirm model/version).
- Firewall/NAT: the bridge must be able to dial Redwood ingress IPs. If you prefer, we can use AWS PrivateLink or GCP VPC-SC to avoid public egress.

Attestation and session lifecycle:
- Attestation flow: bridge performs remote attestation (TPM quote or SGX quote). The bridge includes an attestation statement and an ephemeral public key in the TLS client cert. Redwood validates the attestation via the attestation service and maps the ephemeral key to a tenant session ID.
- Session tokens: ephemeral tokens valid for the session lifetime (default: 30 minutes), rotated on reconnect. Long-running jobs must re-attest to get new tokens.

Sealed blob & backup:
- Sealed blobs: Redwood will persist only encrypted references; the wrapping key can be generated inside your HSM so Redwood cannot unwrap without an explicit escrow operation (requires a multisig HSM policy or an approved KMS request).
- Backup/restore: we recommend an exportable sealed-blob package that you keep offline; restoration requires an HSM unwrap operation and proof-of-possession from the bridge. We'll document the restore runbook in the POC deliverables.

I'll prepare a short network ACL template and a minimal IAM policy for the bridge. Anything else you want validated in the POC?

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple clarifications from our security team: 

1) Backup/restore: when you say 'exportable sealed-blob package', can you confirm the package contains no unwrapped key material and that the restore requires an HSM-held master wrapping key? We need explicit language that Redwood cannot decrypt those blobs without an HSM unwrap operation controlled by DataSyn.
2) Escrow: does Redwood provide an optional escrow mechanism (e.g., split-key escrow held across two operator-controlled HSMs) for disaster recovery, or must the customer retain full sole custody? If escrow is supported, we need details for the governance model (who can trigger unwrap, audit logs, and emergency procedures).

If you can put those assurances in writing for the POC deliverable, we can move forward. Also please add estimated timeline and a brief list of required firewall changes.

Kendall
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Kendall Reyes <kendall@datasyn.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator Bridge POC & attestation checklist

Kendall — short answers and next steps below. We'll include the legal/controls language in the POC statement of work.

1) Backup/restore: confirmed — the exportable sealed-blob package contains only ciphertext and metadata (no plaintext). Restoration requires an HSM unwrap operation using a wrapping key that is generated and stored in your HSM. Redwood cannot unwrap or access plaintext without an unwrap transaction that is cryptographically authorized by your HSM policy (we'll include sample HSM policy statements).

2) Escrow: we support an optional split-key escrow model for customers that want a recovery path. Escrow options:
   - Customer-only custody: no third-party escrow; customer controls all unwrap operations.
   - Split-key escrow: two HSMs (customer-controlled) or one customer + one Redwood escrow HSM protected by strict governance (DocuSign + dual-operator approval). In all escrow modes unwrapping requires multi-step approval and is logged with a signed audit record.

Estimated timeline (POC):
- Week 0 (prep): network ACL template, bridge AMI/container image, vendor HSM port matrix.
- Week 1: deploy bridge in staging VPC; run attestation and basic sign/verify tests.
- Week 2: run audit log collection, backup/restore rehearsal, and produce attestation report.

Firewall changes (minimal):
- Allow outbound TLS to: 34.201.12.45:443 (Redwood ingress edge) and 34.201.12.46:443 (backup edge).
- Allow bridge host access to local HSM vendor ports (we will supply exact port list after you confirm the HSM model).

Next steps: I can send a short SOW + DocuSign for approval and proposed POC dates (we're available starting 2026-05-18). Please confirm preferred dates and whether you want split-key escrow enabled for the POC.

Regards,
